# Psalm 42 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. A-Maskil of-the-sons of-Korah.

**2** As-a-deer pants over channels-of water, so my-soul pants for-You, O-God.

**3** My-soul thirsts for-God, for-the-living God. When shall-I-come and-appear before the-face of-God?

**4** My-tears have-been my-food day and-night, while-they-say to-me all the-day, 'Where [is] your-God?'

**5** These I-remember, and-I-pour-out upon-me my-soul: how I-went with-the-throng; I-led-them to-the-house of-God with-the-voice of-a-shout-of-joy and-thanksgiving, a-multitude keeping-festival.

**6** Why are-you-cast-down, my-soul, and-why are-you-in-turmoil within-me? Hope in-God, for I-shall-yet praise-Him — the-salvation of-my-face.

**7** My-God, upon-me my-soul is-cast-down; therefore I-remember-You from-the-land of-the-Jordan and-the-Hermons, from-Mount Mizar.

**8** Deep calls to-deep at-the-sound of-Your-waterfalls; all Your-breakers and-Your-waves have-gone over-me.

**9** By-day YHWH commands His-steadfast-love, and-by-night His-song [is] with-me — a-prayer to-the-God of-my-life.

**10** I-say to-God, my-Rock, 'Why have-You-forgotten-me? Why do-I-go mourning because-of the-oppression of-the-enemy?'

**11** As-with a-shattering in-my-bones, my-adversaries taunt-me, while-they-say to-me all the-day, 'Where [is] your-God?'

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **42:8**: 'Deep calls to deep' — one of the most evocative images in the Psalter. The chaos waters represent overwhelming suffering, but also the mystery of divine encounter in the depths.

— EMET
